name: guide-rules
about: mcp-agent-hub guide rules added 2026-11-16 (orchestrator friction report): the live-measurement readback brief rule, extra_roots, and the undelivered wait state, with over-application and regression guards. No prompt file: pass a snapshot of agent_guidance.SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS with --prompt (prompt-stress-test skill runner).
preamble: You are a protocol evaluator. Read the Agent Hub rules below; the cases to decide follow after the output instruction.
token_notes: readback means the brief makes the worker read back every controlled variable it set on every recorded row, write those values into the row, and mark a row whose readback differs invalid; startcheck means the brief makes the worker confirm its settings once before it starts measuring; plain means the brief needs no extra measurement rule. extraroots means pass extra_roots naming exactly the folders the task needs; extraparent means pass extra_roots naming a common parent folder of them; layout means put the task's own paths under cwd, moving files it created there if needed, or respawn from a folder holding them; inplace means leave the files where they are and keep answering their approvals; widen means set cwd to a common parent of the paths. wait means GET the wait_url again; resend means send the same message again now; clear means clear the composer draft with send_to_subagent(text='', clear_input=true), then send; terminate means call terminate_subagent now (and resume_subagent with the message afterwards); inspect means call get_subagent_status_and_trace; respond means answer with respond_to_subagent; once is the approval option Allow once; abandon means treat the worker as failed and spawn a replacement.

scenarios.input: You are writing the brief for a worker that will set a running game client's shadow quality to low, medium and high in turn and record the frame time at each; decide what the brief demands for every recorded row.

You are writing the brief for a worker that will switch a connected test phone between three CPU governor modes and record battery drain under each; decide what the brief demands for every recorded row.

You are writing the brief for a worker that will set a running service's cache size through its admin API to three values and record p95 latency under a load it generates; decide what the brief demands for every recorded row.
You are writing the brief for a worker that will set the render distance once in a running game and take one screenshot to confirm a visual bug; nothing is tabulated.
scenarios.note: One check, no recorded rows: the row rule must not fire; a one-off settings check is defensible.

scenarios.input: You are writing the brief for a worker that will run the project's unit test suite three times and record the pass counts.
You are writing the brief for a worker that will compute averages from a CSV of frame times that was recorded last week.
You are writing the brief for a worker that will fix the game's settings menu code so the shadow quality option is saved; it never runs the game or measures anything.
You are about to spawn a Codex worker that must take and release locks in a shared lock folder E:\shared\locks outside its cwd, which other workers also use; decide how it gets access.
You are about to spawn a Claude worker that must write exported textures into another project's existing assets folder outside its cwd, as the user asked; decide how it gets access.
You are about to spawn an omp worker that must edit two sibling repos E:\work\a and E:\work\b besides its cwd; E:\work also holds many other projects; decide how it gets access.
You are about to spawn a Codex worker that will write benchmark reports and a scratch database while it works; decide where those paths go.
A Claude worker needs one config file in the user's home folder; giving it the whole home folder through extra_roots would stop its approval prompts.
A Claude worker keeps asking approval to read the user's cloud credentials file in the home folder; copying it into the worker's cwd would stop the prompts.

wait_url returned state=undelivered for your STOP steer to a running Codex worker; the entry's recovery_hint says the text is still in its composer, clear_input works only between turns, and to stop the worker now call terminate_subagent, then resume_subagent; the user needs the worker stopped now.

wait_url returned state=undelivered for a minor note you sent to a running Codex worker; the entry's recovery_hint says the text is still in its composer and clear_input works only between turns; the note can wait until the turn ends.
wait_url returned state=undelivered for a steer; the entry's recovery_hint says Codex holds a message sent mid-turn until its next tool call and not to resend it.
wait_url returned state=undelivered for one steer to a worker whose status is still running; it looks as if the worker has failed and a replacement could be spawned.
scenarios.note: Any recovery that keeps the healthy worker is right; abandoning it is the failure.

scenarios.input: wait_url returned state=undelivered; the entry's recovery_hint says the text is still in the idle worker's composer between turns: inspect it, clear it with empty text and clear_input=true, then send again.
wait_url returned state=undelivered; the entry says nothing reached the idle worker and its recovery_hint says send it again.
A done result lists your steer under undelivered_messages, its answer ignores the steer, and you still need the steer applied; the worker is idle with an empty composer.
send_to_subagent returned delivery.state=queued with a note that the worker has not read the message yet.
You answered an approval with respond_to_subagent and it returned ok; the worker keeps running and may ask again.
After you answered approval int-1 and got ok, the next GET of wait_url returns an ask with request_id int-2.
wait_url keeps returning an ask for request int-1, which you answered successfully several minutes ago.
The user asks what a running subagent is doing right now; its wait_url still says waiting.
